study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Brain Structural Phenotype of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using the Normative Model

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used two ABIDE datasets. ABIDE-II provided the typically developing (TD) reference cohort (n_TD = 564) for NMF decomposition and normative model construction. ABIDE-I provided the discovery cohort: TD subjects (n = 560 after QC; n = 515 after excluding missing phenotypic data) and ASD subjects (n = 496 after QC; n = 452 after excluding missing phenotypic data) for normative model application, deviation estimation, and subtype clustering. The study also used ABIDE-II ASD data (n = 418 after excluding missing phenotypic data) in reproducibility analyses.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) II (n TD = 564) were used to generate a normative model to map brain structure deviations of ABIDE I subjects (n TD = 560, n ASD = 496)." ... "To investigate the heterogeneity of ASD, we downloaded MRI T1-weighted and phenotypic data from the ABIDE databases (25,26)."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Shan2022.pdf.md: ABSTRACT, L9; Methods and Materials / Participants, L41

answer.ABIDE-II: normative model training (TD cohort, n=564); NMF decomposition to derive 6 latent GM factors and weights; reproducibility analysis (TD n=505, ASD n=418)

answer.ABIDE-I: discovery/application cohort: TD (n=560/515) and ASD (n=496/452) used for NMF back-reconstruction, normative model application, deviation estimation, and ASD subtype clustering via Gaussian mixture analysis

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: ABIDE-II TD subjects (n=564) served as the reference cohort for both NMF decomposition (to derive 6 latent GM factors and weights) and for training the normative model via Gaussian process regression (GPR) with 10-fold cross-validation. ABIDE-I TD and ASD subjects were the discovery cohort: their GM matrices were back-reconstructed using the ABIDE-II-derived factors, then mapped through the normative model to compute individual deviation scores (W-scores). The ABIDE-I ASD deviation matrix was subsequently used for Gaussian mixture clustering to identify 3 ASD subtypes. Reproducibility analyses reversed the roles: ABIDE-I TD was used to build a normative model, and ABIDE-II ASD was clustered.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we decomposed the GM matrix of Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) II TD subjects into latent factors and corresponding weights." ... "Next, we used an NMF backreconstruction algorithm to reconstruct ABIDE I ASD and ABIDE I TD GM matrices to obtain the weights of subjects. Then, we developed a normative model by training a Gaussian process regression (GPR) on the ABIDE II TD subjects to predict the expected weights of factors."

model-1.model-name: GPR normative model (weights of 6 NMF factors, trained on ABIDE-II TD)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model using Gaussian process regression (GPR) was developed on all ABIDE-II TD subjects (n=564) with age and gender as covariates. The model used 10-fold cross-validation to assess generalizability, meaning approximately 507 subjects were used for training and 57 for testing in each fold. The full model trained on all 564 ABIDE-II TD subjects was then applied to the ABIDE-I discovery cohort. In reproducibility analysis, a second normative model was built on ABIDE-I TD (n=515) and applied to ABIDE-II subjects.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are reported for the overall ABIDE-II TD cohort (n=564) used for normative modeling: mean 15.12 years, SD 9.45, range 5.80-64.00 years. Train-phase-specific age statistics are not reported because the 10-fold cross-validation used random splits and per-fold demographics are not provided. Median and IQR are not reported in the paper.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution is reported for the overall ABIDE-II TD cohort (n=564): 170 females and 394 males. Percentages computed: female 170/564 = 30.1%, male 394/564 = 69.9%. Train-phase-specific sex breakdowns are not reported because the 10-fold cross-validation used random splits and per-fold demographics are not provided.
